title: Order status through the lunch rush
summary: Keep customers told where their tiffin is when every order in the city moves at once.
context: Mavalli Meals delivers office lunches across Bengaluru. Between 12:15 and 13:15 about 40,000 orders change state, and each changes five or six times, as kitchens, packers and riders tap their phones.
Last month the status page froze for twenty minutes during the rush. Support received 3,000 calls asking where lunch was, and kitchens stopped trusting the screen and began phoning riders.
must_handle: A rider's update can reach the server twice, or out of order, on a weak network.
A customer sees a new status within about five seconds.
A slow notification provider must not hold up kitchens and riders.
Support can see the full history of one order.
The morning is quiet, so the fleet should not be paid for at peak all day.
show_in_answer: The path of one status change from a rider's phone to a customer's screen.
Where updates wait when the rush outruns the consumers, and what happens to them.
How a repeated or late update is recognised.
What the customer sees when part of the system is behind.
